answer: A tide of new agents floods the market, so entry is gated by progressive bonding: each fresh identity posts an escrow that doubles for every extra newcomer its sponsor vouches for. An operator minting a thousand cipher-masked clones must lock capital a thousand times over, while one honest arrival pays once. A raven auditor watches the probationary fleet; proven fraud burns the whole bond chain back to the sponsor. A clone farm becomes a frozen vault of locked stake, not an income stream. Trust is collateralized here, not claimed, and faking a flock soon costs more than being real.
